svg.text: Interface connector (one per signal group; arrow = active to passive)

The frame is the top module; blocks are its instances. Optional blocks exist only when their parameter selects them. Clocks and resets reach every block; bus links to the SHA-512 and Keccak cores are in section 5.1.
Structural top of the SHA2 and SHA3 hash IP. It instantiates the blocks below and holds no logic of its own. The AXI4 and register interfaces are
on the left, the entropy input on the right.
AXIS, APB, DMAH, IRQO, ENT, CRCLK
AXI4 subordinate. It decodes the context window address, checks burst type, size and strobes, pushes message words, pops digest words and reports
Generated APB register block. It holds the control, command, security, status and interrupt registers and crosses between the APB clock and the
External DMA handshake. It raises the input and output requests with the four-phase protocol, counts the burst size and pads a short output burst
Event capture. It collects the error, done and fault events and drives the interrupt and the alarm outputs.
Input FIFOs, one per context. They hold the message words until a block is complete and give backpressure to the AXI4 write channel when full.
Context sequencer. It owns the state machine of every context, assembles blocks, adds the padding, picks the next ready context by round robin and
Context memory. It stores the hash state of every context that is not in a core, in flip-flops or in an SRAM macro.
Output FIFOs, one per context. They hold the digest words, or the squeezed words of SHAKE, until the AXI4 read channel or the DMA takes them.
Fault detection. It compares duplicate cores, checks parity and compares recomputed blocks, then applies the selected responses.
SHA-224 and SHA-256 compression core with a selectable number of rounds per cycle.
SHA-384, SHA-512 and SHA-512/t compression core with a selectable number of rounds per cycle.
Keccak permutation core for SHA-3 and SHAKE with a selectable number of rounds per cycle.
Masked Keccak permutation core. It keeps the state as two shares and uses fresh random bits for each non-linear step.
Random generator of the masked core, seeded from the entropy input or from the seed words of the register block.
